# Communicative lesson brief: Make and reschedule the appointment

## Role in the unit

This is the application lesson in the doctor-appointment unit. It follows the
reusable grammar package at `../grammar/`, whose source slug is
`question_word_order`.

The prerequisite explains a form. This lesson teaches the learner to choose a
useful response as the other speaker provides information. It is an
interaction, not a script and not a fixed procedure.

## Primary objective

The learner can handle a short appointment call by giving a reason, making a
request, responding appropriately to an offered time, and reaching a clear
arrangement when the first option is unavailable.

## Interaction contract

The model should show a realistic exchange with roles and enough context to
understand what each speaker knows. The learner should be able to choose among
responses such as:

- explaining why they are calling;
- asking for an appointment;
- accepting an offered time when it works;
- saying that an offered time is unavailable and asking about another one;
- asking for clarification when a day or time was not heard; and
- confirming the arrangement once both speakers understand it.

These are communicative resources, not a required order. The next response
depends on what the other speaker has just said.

## Language resources

Reuse the grammar lesson's question as a ready-made resource:
`Kan jeg få en time på torsdag?` The communicative lesson may also use
`Jeg vil gjerne bestille en time`, `Torsdag passer ikke for meg`, and
`Da ses vi på fredag klokka ni`.

These phrases support the interaction. Do not add a grammar lecture about
finite verbs, modal verbs, or V2 here. Link the learner back to the grammar
package when an explanation is needed.

## Changed condition

The model call offers Thursday. In the final task, Thursday is unavailable to
the learner and Friday is the proposed alternative. The point is to respond to
the changed availability, not to recite the model call.

## Acceptance criteria

- The lesson opens with a complete, understandable interaction in context.
- Practice covers request, availability, alternative, clarification, and
  confirmation choices without presenting them as a prescribed sequence.
- The final task changes the availability condition.
- The compiled lesson contains no claim that it teaches Norwegian word order;
  that belongs to the prerequisite grammar lesson.
- The final closed `build` remains labelled as a constrained transfer proxy,
  not open conversational performance.
